newsitem.title: USA: Dow, Nasdaq rally to record highs; bonds, dollar rise.
newsitem.headline: Dow, Nasdaq rally to record highs; bonds, dollar rise.

text.p: Stocks surged to a new record close on Wednesday, as an upturn in the bond market soothed investor worries about a resurgence of inflation.
The dollar climbed to a new eight-year high against the German mark, and corn and soybean prices also rose.

After four straight lackluster sessions, blue-chip stocks shook off their summer doldrums, aided by the first drop in long-term interest rates in the bond market in four sessions. The Dow Jones industrial average rose 71.77 points to 8,259.31, a record, eclipsing the old mark of 8,254.89 set last Wednesday.

Technology issues got a boost from a surprise peace pact between former bitter rivals Apple Computer Inc. and Microsoft Corp. The Nasdaq composite index, laden with high-tech stocks, rose 8.91 to 1,630.44, also a new high.
"I think today probably surprised even the bulls and helped batter the bears," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons.

Investors said blue-chip issues benefitted from signs of stability in the bond market. Long-term rates had jumped since Friday after unexpectedly strong economic reports pointed to inflationary pressures building in the economy.
"This is the first day bonds have stabilised," said Bruce Bittles, market strategist at J.C. Bradford. "That helped the market."
The 30-year Treasury rose an eighth of a point, or $1.25 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, to 6.48 percent from 6.49 percent on Tuesday.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat decliners 1,836 to 976 on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 565 million shares.

The market also got a boost from startling news that Apple and Microsoft were ending their bitter rivalry, with Microsoft investing $150 million in Apple, which had racked up more than $1.6 billion in losses over the past 18 months.
Apple jumped 6-9/16 to 26-5/16 and was the most active issue on Nasdaq stock. Microsoft rose 1/8 to 143-7/16.

Meanwhile, the dollar posted its fourth straight eight-year high against the German mark amid fresh signs of German economic weakness. But it slipped against the Japanese yen on rising U.S.-Japanese trade tensions.
The dollar reached an intraday high of 1.8913 marks, its highest since October 1989, before settling in New York at 1.8820 marks, up from 1.8795 late on Tuesday.
Against the yen, the dollar reached an intraday high of 119.58, the strongest since May 12, but ended lower at 118.70 yen from 119.25 yen late on Tuesday.
In commodity markets, corn and soybean prices rose after forecasters predicted more dry weather for parched fields in the Midwest.
At the Chicago Board of Trade, soybeans delivery in November rose 15-1/2 cents a bushel to close at $6.50. December corn closed 4-1/4 cents higher at $2.61-1/2.
Overseas, Britain's FTSE 100 closed at 5,026.2, up 65.6 points, or 1.32 percent. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average ended at 19,702.07, up 187.62 points, or 0.96 percent.
